key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Subacute, over days to weeks. LOCATION: Generalized systemic symptoms. DURATION: Continuous over weeks. CHARACTER: Fever, fatigue, malaise, night sweats. AGGRAVATING: None specific. RELIEVING: Antibiotics. TIMING: Progressive, worsening. SEVERITY: Variable systemic illness. KEY POSITIVES: Persistent fever, new or changing heart murmur, IVDU (injection drug use), recent dental work or procedure, prosthetic valve, splinter hemorrhages, Osler nodes, Janeway lesions, embolic phenomena (stroke, splenic infarct). KEY NEGATIVES: NOT acute onset, NOT isolated chest pain.
